day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 13:00. Take the Magical Express or a budget rideshare (Lyft/Uber) to your boutique stay near Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented. Pick up a Disney park map and plan your week. Walk around the hotel area and explore the resort grounds to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Disney Springs (free admission, no park ticket required) via complimentary Disney bus shuttle. Browse the shops, enjoy live entertainment, and soak in the Disney atmosphere. Great way to ease into the trip without spending on park tickets.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or during your flight to save money
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the airport — Subway or McDonald's airside to stay budget-friendly
meals.dinner: Disney Springs: Try Earl of Sandwich for a filling, affordable meal (~$10–$12 per person) or grab a quick-service meal at Chicken Guy! by Guy Fieri

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a multi-day Disney park ticket in advance online for the best savings. Consider the Disney Value Ticket option or check for AAA/military discounts. Download the My Disney Experience app to manage park reservations and Lightning Lane passes.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Magic Kingdom early (park opens at 9:00 AM — arrive by 8:30 AM for rope drop). Head straight to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain and Buzz Lightyear's Space Ranger Spin before crowds build. Then loop to Fantasyland for Seven Dwarfs Mine Train using the My Disney Experience app to grab Lightning Lane if needed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Adventureland — Pirates of the Caribbean and Jungle Cruise are must-dos. Take a break during peak afternoon heat (1–3 PM) at a shaded area or air-conditioned attraction like the Carousel of Progress. Visit Liberty Square and ride Haunted Mansion.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the Magic Kingdom evening spectacular — 'Disney Enchantment' or the current nighttime parade and fireworks show (check the app for exact schedule). This is included in your park ticket and is absolutely unmissable. Exit after the fireworks when crowds thin.

meals.breakfast: Eat a hearty breakfast at your hotel before heading out to save money and energy
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square — affordable counter-service with clam chowder, fish & chips (~$12–$15 per person)
meals.dinner: Cosmic Ray's Starlight Café in Tomorrowland — budget-friendly burgers, chicken, and sandwiches (~$12–$14 per person). Eat before the fireworks show.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes and bring a refillable water bottle — free water is available at any quick-service location. Arrive early for rope drop to maximize ride time before lines grow. Use the Lightning Lane Multi Pass strategically for top-tier attractions.

day_by_day.morning: Head to EPCOT for rope drop (typically 9:00 AM). Start in World Discovery — ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (book Individual Lightning Lane early via the app at 7:00 AM). Then hit Test Track and Mission: SPACE for a full space-themed morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore World Nature — Journey of Water and Soarin' Around the World are highlights. Then stroll through the World Showcase beginning at 12:00 PM when it opens. Walk through Mexico, Norway (ride Frozen Ever After), and continue around the lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT's 'EPCOT Forever' or 'Luminous the Symphony of Us' nighttime lagoon show (check current schedule on My Disney Experience app). Enjoy the World Showcase atmosphere with street food snacks from various countries.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pack granola bars and fruit from a nearby grocery store to save money
meals.lunch: Sunshine Seasons in The Land pavilion — one of EPCOT's best budget quick-service options with fresh, affordable meals (~$12–$15 per person)
meals.dinner: World Showcase food stands — budget tip: share 2–3 small plates from different countries (Mexico, Japan, Morocco) for a fun and affordable international dinner (~$15–$20 per person total)

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is very walkable but large — comfortable footwear is essential. The World Showcase is perfect for leisurely exploration. Cosmic Rewind Lightning Lane sells out fast — book at exactly 7:00 AM in the app. Bring a portable phone charger.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hollywood Studios for rope drop. Head immediately to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge — ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run (standby line is usually manageable at rope drop). Then get in the virtual queue or Lightning Lane for Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance, one of the most immersive rides at Disney.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Toy Story Land — Slinky Dog Dash and Alien Swirling Saucers are great fun. Then catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular (check show times). Visit the Twilight Zone Tower of Terror and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster for thrill seekers.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the 'Fantasmic!' nighttime show at the Hollywood Hills Amphitheater (check schedule — usually 8:00 PM or 9:00 PM). This is a spectacular free-with-admission show featuring water, fire, and Disney characters. Great way to end the day.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Woody's Lunch Box in Toy Story Land — fun theming and affordable comfort food like grilled cheese and tots (~$11–$13 per person)
meals.dinner: Backlot Express near Star Wars land — counter-service burgers, chicken strips, and sandwiches (~$12–$15 per person). Eat before the Fantasmic! show.

day_by_day.notes: Hollywood Studios is the most 'ride-dense' park — plan your Lightning Lane selections carefully. Rise of the Resistance is a bucket-list experience; prioritize it. June weather in Orlando is hot and humid — stay hydrated and take indoor breaks during peak afternoon heat.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Disney's Animal Kingdom for rope drop. Head straight to Pandora – The World of Avatar. Ride Avatar Flight of Passage first thing (lines grow quickly — this is the most popular ride in the park). Then ride Na'vi River Journey for a calmer Pandora experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Africa — ride Kilimanjaro Safaris in the early afternoon for best animal activity. Walk the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail for free wildlife viewing. Head to Asia for Expedition Everest and Kali River Rapids (expect to get wet — great for hot June weather).
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the 'Rivers of Light' or 'Tree of Life Awakenings' evening experience (check current show schedule). The Tree of Life projections are stunning and free with park admission. Animal Kingdom typically closes earlier than other parks — plan accordingly.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pack snacks
meals.lunch: Flame Tree Barbecue in Discovery Island — one of Disney's best quick-service meals with ribs, chicken, and pulled pork in a beautiful waterfront setting (~$13–$16 per person)
meals.dinner: Satu'li Canteen in Pandora — healthy, customizable bowls with protein and grains, great value for a Disney quick-service meal (~$14–$17 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom is best experienced in the morning when animals are most active. Kali River Rapids will get you soaking wet — bring a change of clothes or wear quick-dry clothing. Check park closing time as it's often earlier (8:00–9:00 PM) than other Disney parks.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. This is your flex/recovery day. Visit a nearby budget-friendly attraction: check out Disney's BoardWalk (free to walk around) along the waterfront between EPCOT and Hollywood Studios. Enjoy the street performers and lakeside views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to your favorite park for a half-day visit using your multi-day ticket. Alternatively, explore Disney Springs again for shopping, free entertainment, and people-watching. Visit the LEGO Store, World of Disney shop (browsing is free!), and enjoy live music along the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner tonight as a mid-trip treat. Disney Springs offers several mid-range options. Alternatively, head back to a park for evening rides when crowds are lower and temperatures drop.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed hotel breakfast — pick up groceries from a nearby Publix or Walmart (accessible by rideshare) for affordable in-room snacks and breakfast items to save money throughout the trip
meals.lunch: Disney Springs: Blaze Fast-Fire'd Pizza — build-your-own pizza for ~$10–$12, fast and filling
meals.dinner: Disney Springs: The Polite Pig — BBQ smokehouse with reasonable prices for a sit-down experience (~$18–$22 per person). Treat yourself — you've earned it!

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to recharge your feet and energy for the final day push. Stock up on affordable snacks at a grocery store to reduce in-park food spending on your last day. Check your My Disney Experience app for any park reservations needed for Day 7.

day_by_day.morning: Return to your favorite park one last time for rope drop. Use any remaining Lightning Lane passes or revisit must-do attractions you want to experience again. Magic Kingdom is a popular final-day choice for its iconic atmosphere and farewell fireworks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dedicate the afternoon to final rides, souvenir shopping (budget tip: shop at Disney Springs or the park exit gift shops for the best selection — avoid impulse buying mid-park). Take photos at iconic spots: Cinderella Castle, the EPCOT geodesphere, or Hollywood Studios' Chinese Theatre.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening at Magic Kingdom — stay for the last fireworks show of your trip. 'Disney Enchantment' over Cinderella Castle is the perfect send-off. Take a final walk down Main Street USA and soak it all in before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Use up any remaining in-room groceries or grab a quick hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Casey's Corner on Main Street USA, Magic Kingdom — classic hot dogs and corn dog nuggets, very affordable (~$10–$12 per person) and a Disney tradition
meals.dinner: Pecos Bill Tall Tale Inn and Cafe in Frontierland, Magic Kingdom — nachos, tacos, and burgers (~$12–$15 per person). Dine early before the final fireworks crowd surge.

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags the night before if you have an early departure on June 22. Store luggage at the hotel bell desk if needed for a late checkout. Budget tip: your biggest savings came from rope-drop strategy, quick-service dining, free Disney Springs evenings, and advance ticket purchases — great job staying budget-conscious! Total estimated daily in-park food budget: $35–$50 per adult using quick-service dining.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Use this time to travel from the airport to your Boutique Stay in Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista. Take Disney's Magical Express or a rideshare (~30-45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with resort maps and park apps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disney Springs Exploration: Head to Disney Springs (free admission, no park ticket needed) to ease into the Disney atmosphere. Browse the shops, grab a snack, and soak in the entertainment. Great way to recover from travel without the intensity of a full park day.
day_by_day.evening: Disney Springs Dining & Entertainment Evening: Enjoy a leisurely stroll through Disney Springs, catch a live performance or street entertainer, and pick up any last-minute supplies (sunscreen, ponchos) at World of Disney store.

meals.breakfast: Grab a bite at the airport or on the plane before landing.
meals.lunch: Lunch on arrival — try Blaze Fast-Fire'd Pizza or D-Luxe Burger at Disney Springs for a quick, affordable mid-range meal (~$15-20 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Boathouse or STK Orlando at Disney Springs — mid-range splurge to kick off the trip (~$30-50 per person). Alternatively, Frontera Cocina for Mexican cuisine at a slightly lower price point.

day_by_day.notes: Download the My Disney Experience app before arrival. Link your park tickets and set up Disney MagicMobile. Purchase a refillable resort mug if you plan to use resort dining. Arrive at Disney Springs by 3:00 PM to maximize the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park – Early Entry & Iconic Rides: Arrive at rope drop (park opens ~9:00 AM, Early Theme Park Entry at 8:30 AM for resort guests). Head straight to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain, then Fantasyland for Seven Dwarfs Mine Train using Lightning Lane if needed. Ride Pirates of the Caribbean and The Haunted Mansion before crowds build.
day_by_day.afternoon: Magic Kingdom Park – Continued Adventure: Explore Liberty Square and Frontierland — ride Big Thunder Mountain Railroad and splash through Splash Mountain (check current status). Watch the Festival of Fantasy Parade (typically ~3:00 PM). Take a mid-afternoon break at the resort if needed (resort proximity is a big advantage).
day_by_day.evening: Magic Kingdom Fireworks & Castle Show: Return to Magic Kingdom for the evening. Secure a viewing spot on Main Street U.S.A. for the Happily Ever After fireworks spectacular (check schedule). End the night with a stroll down Main Street before park close.

meals.breakfast: Resort hotel breakfast or grab a quick bite at Main Street Bakery (Starbucks partnership) inside Magic Kingdom (~$10-15).
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square — affordable counter service with fish, chicken, and sandwiches (~$15-18 per person).
meals.dinner: Be Our Guest Restaurant in Fantasyland (prix-fixe dinner, book in advance via My Disney Experience, ~$62 per adult) OR Tony's Town Square Restaurant on Main Street (~$30-40 per person) for a more relaxed mid-range option.

day_by_day.notes: This is the flagship park — plan to spend a full day here. Use Lightning Lane Multi Pass for top attractions. Wear comfortable shoes. Stay hydrated — Orlando in June is hot and humid (expect 90°F+). Resort guests get Early Theme Park Entry (30 min before general public).

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT – Future World & Guardians of the Galaxy: Arrive at EPCOT for rope drop. Use Early Entry to ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (Lightning Lane Individual highly recommended — purchase at 7:00 AM). Also ride Test Track and Soarin' Around the World in the morning before lines build.
day_by_day.afternoon: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour: Begin exploring the 11 country pavilions starting around noon. Sample food and drinks from Mexico, Norway, China, Germany, Italy, America, Japan, Morocco, France, United Kingdom, and Canada. This is a leisurely, immersive cultural experience perfect for families.
day_by_day.evening: EPCOT World Showcase – Evening & EPCOT Forever: Continue grazing through World Showcase pavilions. Watch the EPCOT Forever nighttime spectacular over the lagoon (~9:00 PM). The view from the France or United Kingdom pavilion is especially scenic.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the resort before heading out.
meals.lunch: World Showcase grazing lunch — try a Ramen bowl from Japan (~$12), a Crepe from France (~$10), and a School Bread from Norway (~$6). Budget ~$25-35 per person for a satisfying World Showcase lunch.
meals.dinner: Sit-down dinner at Teppan Edo (Japanese hibachi, Japan Pavilion, ~$35-50 per person, reservations recommended) OR La Hacienda de San Angel (Mexican, lakeside views, ~$35-45 per person).

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is best enjoyed at a relaxed pace. Wear a comfortable bag for snacks and souvenirs. The World Showcase opens at 11:00 AM. Book dining reservations 60 days in advance via My Disney Experience. EPCOT is one of the most walkable parks — plan for 4-6 miles of walking.

day_by_day.morning: Hollywood Studios – Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Adventure: Arrive at rope drop with Early Entry. Head directly to Galaxy's Edge — ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run first (shorter wait in the morning). If budget allows, book the Rise of the Resistance Lightning Lane Individual ($25-30 per person) — it's worth every penny. Explore the immersive land atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hollywood Studios – Build a Lightsaber & More: Visit Savi's Workshop to build a custom lightsaber (~$249.99 per lightsaber — optional splurge, book well in advance). Alternatively, build a custom droid at Droid Depot (~$119.99). Also ride Slinky Dog Dash in Toy Story Land and catch the Fantasmic! show (check schedule).
day_by_day.evening: Hollywood Studios – Tower of Terror & Nighttime: Ride The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster Starring Aerosmith in the evening when crowds thin. Watch the Star Wars: A Galactic Spectacular fireworks show if scheduled. Depart after the show.

meals.breakfast: Grab a Ronto Wrap from Ronto Roasters in Galaxy's Edge — a beloved Star Wars breakfast option (~$14).
meals.lunch: Docking Bay 7 Food and Cargo in Galaxy's Edge — themed counter service with creative dishes (~$16-22 per person).
meals.dinner: 50's Prime Time Café — fun retro diner atmosphere with classic American comfort food (~$25-35 per person, reservations recommended) OR Sci-Fi Dine-In Theater for a unique drive-in movie experience (~$25-35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Hollywood Studios is the most thrill-ride-heavy park. Lightning Lane purchases are highly recommended here. Galaxy's Edge is extremely popular — arrive early. The park can feel crowded in June; use the app to monitor wait times and plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Animal Kingdom – Kilimanjaro Safaris: Arrive at rope drop for Early Entry. Head straight to Kilimanjaro Safaris — animals are most active in the cooler morning hours, making this the best time for wildlife viewing. See lions, elephants, giraffes, rhinos, and more. Then ride Expedition Everest nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Animal Kingdom – Avatar Flight of Passage & Pandora: Head to Pandora – The World of Avatar. Ride Avatar: Flight of Passage (Lightning Lane Individual strongly recommended — one of the best rides in all of Disney World). Explore the bioluminescent world of Pandora and ride Na'vi River Journey. Take time to enjoy the incredible theming and landscaping.
day_by_day.evening: Animal Kingdom – Tree of Life & Rivers of Light: Watch the Tree of Life Awakenings projection show at dusk (check schedule). If available, catch Rivers of Light or an evening show. Explore Discovery Island before heading back to the resort for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or Starbucks before park entry.
meals.lunch: Satu'li Canteen in Pandora — one of the best counter-service restaurants in all of Disney World. Try the Cheeseburger Steamed Pods or Grain Bowl (~$16-20 per person).
meals.dinner: Yak & Yeti Restaurant in Asia — Asian-fusion cuisine in a beautiful setting (~$25-40 per person, reservations recommended). OR Tiffins Restaurant for a more upscale, signature dining experience (~$50-70 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom closes earlier than other parks (typically 8:00-9:00 PM). Plan your day accordingly. Wear light, breathable clothing — the park involves a lot of outdoor walking. Bring bug spray for the evening. Flight of Passage is a must-do — secure Lightning Lane early.

day_by_day.morning: Resort Day & Pool Time: Take a well-deserved rest day from the parks. Enjoy the resort's amenities — pool, lazy river, or any on-site activities. This is especially important for families with younger children who may be experiencing park fatigue. Sleep in and have a leisurely breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Magic Kingdom – Revisit Favorites or Catch Missed Rides: Return to Magic Kingdom for a half-day afternoon visit. Use this time to ride anything you missed on Day 2, or re-ride favorites. Check for updated Lightning Lane availability. Visit the Carousel of Progress, Tomorrowland Speedway, or Dumbo the Flying Elephant for younger guests.
day_by_day.evening: Magic Kingdom – Dessert Party & Fireworks: Book a Fireworks Dessert Party (if budget allows, ~$99-109 per adult, ~$59-69 per child) for a premium reserved viewing spot for the Happily Ever After fireworks with unlimited desserts and beverages. A magical way to celebrate the second-to-last night.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant leisurely breakfast — enjoy the downtime. Try the resort's full breakfast spread (~$15-25 per person).
meals.lunch: Cosmic Ray's Starlight Café (Magic Kingdom counter service) — burgers, chicken, and salads at great value (~$12-16 per person).
meals.dinner: Cinderella's Royal Table inside Cinderella Castle — a bucket-list dining experience (~$60-80 per adult, reservations required 60 days out). Book this well in advance for a truly magical evening.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is typically one of the busiest days at Disney World. If the parks feel overwhelming, lean into the resort day more fully and only do a short park visit. The Dessert Party must be booked in advance via My Disney Experience. This is a great day for souvenir shopping.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT – Revisit or Finish World Showcase: Return to EPCOT for any pavilions or rides missed on Day 3. Ride any remaining Future World attractions. Pick up last-minute souvenirs from the country pavilions. Enjoy a final morning in the parks at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disney Springs – Final Shopping & Farewell: Head to Disney Springs for final souvenir shopping at World of Disney (the largest Disney merchandise store in the world). Browse LEGO Store, Marketplace Co-Op, and other unique shops. This is also a great time for any last-minute purchases and to soak in the final Disney atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Departure Prep: Enjoy a final celebratory dinner at Disney Springs or the resort. Pack up, confirm transportation to the airport for departure, and reminisce on the week's magical experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — treat yourself to a full sit-down meal to fuel the last day (~$15-25 per person).
meals.lunch: Quick-service lunch at EPCOT — revisit a World Showcase favorite or try something new. Budget ~$15-20 per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at The BOATHOUSE at Disney Springs — waterfront dining with American cuisine, steaks, and fresh seafood (~$40-60 per person). A memorable final meal with great ambiance.

day_by_day.notes: Check out of the resort per hotel policy (typically 11:00 AM). Disney Springs can hold luggage if needed. Confirm return transportation to Orlando International Airport — allow at least 2-3 hours before your flight. Consider Disney's Resort Airline Check-In service to check bags at the resort before heading to the airport (available for select airlines).

Enjoy the resort pool, unwind from travel, and let concierge arrange your MagicBand+ setup, Lightning Lane Multi Pass, and dining reservations for the week. Take a leisurely stroll around the resort grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Disney Springs Dining & Entertainment Evening: Head to Disney Springs (complimentary admission) for a curated first-night experience. Browse luxury boutiques, enjoy live entertainment, and soak in the vibrant atmosphere as an ideal low-key introduction to the Disney World resort area.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy in-flight dining or grab a light snack upon landing at MCO
meals.lunch: Chef Art Smith's Homecomin' at Disney Springs — Southern comfort cuisine with premium craft cocktails and a warm, upscale-casual atmosphere
meals.dinner: Morimoto Asia at Disney Springs — Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto's flagship Pan-Asian restaurant offering exquisite sushi, Peking duck, and an extensive sake list in a stunning two-story dining room

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Lightning Lane Individual Attraction Selections and dining reservations 60 days in advance. Ask concierge to pre-stock your room with preferred beverages and snacks. Consider purchasing Disney Genie+ for the full week to maximize ride access with minimal wait times.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park — Early Entry & Iconic Rides: Take advantage of Early Theme Park Entry (30 minutes before official opening) exclusive to resort guests. Head straight to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain, then Seven Dwarfs Mine Train via Lightning Lane. Explore Fantasyland and catch the morning atmosphere before crowds build.
day_by_day.afternoon: Magic Kingdom Continued — Adventureland & Liberty Square: Experience Pirates of the Caribbean, Haunted Mansion, and Big Thunder Mountain Railroad. Enjoy a relaxed mid-afternoon break back at the resort pool to escape peak heat, then return refreshed for the evening spectaculars.
day_by_day.evening: EPCOT Fireworks & Happily Ever After: Return to Magic Kingdom for the world-famous 'Happily Ever After' nighttime spectacular — a breathtaking projection and fireworks show over Cinderella Castle. Secure a premium viewing spot on Main Street U.S.A. or upgrade to a fireworks dessert party for reserved viewing with gourmet treats.

meals.breakfast: The Grand Floridian Café (at the nearby Grand Floridian Resort) — elegant Florida-inspired breakfast with eggs Benedict, fresh-squeezed juices, and pastries in a Victorian setting
meals.lunch: Be Our Guest Restaurant inside Magic Kingdom — dine in the enchanted Beast's Castle with prix-fixe French-inspired cuisine; reserve well in advance
meals.dinner: Cinderella's Royal Table — a once-in-a-lifetime fine dining experience inside Cinderella Castle with princess meet-and-greets, royal décor, and a curated American menu with premium wine selections

day_by_day.notes: Cinderella's Royal Table and Be Our Guest require advance dining reservations (ADR) — book at the 60-day window the moment it opens. The Magic Kingdom Fireworks Dessert Party offers reserved prime viewing and is worth the premium price for a stress-free spectacular experience.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour — Morning Pavilions: Arrive at EPCOT for Early Entry. Begin in Future World with Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (Lightning Lane recommended) and Test Track. Then transition to the World Showcase as pavilions open, starting with the Japan, China, and Morocco pavilions — explore authentic architecture, galleries, and cultural demonstrations.
day_by_day.afternoon: EPCOT World Showcase — Culinary Deep Dive: Spend the afternoon doing a curated food and beverage crawl through the 11 country pavilions. Sample authentic international cuisine — French crepes, Norwegian school bread, Italian gelato, Mexican street corn, and Canadian cheddar cheese soup. Enjoy the living cultural mosaic at a leisurely premium pace.
day_by_day.evening: EPCOT International Food & Wine Festival (if in season) or EPCOT Forever Nighttime Spectacular: Experience EPCOT's signature nighttime show over World Showcase Lagoon featuring fireworks, music, and illuminated kites. Upgrade to the EPCOT Forever Dessert Party for reserved lakeside seating with gourmet desserts and sparkling beverages.

meals.breakfast: Kringla Bakeri Og Kafé in Norway Pavilion — freshly baked pastries, open-faced sandwiches, and Norwegian coffee in a charming Scandinavian setting
meals.lunch: Chefs de France in the France Pavilion — classic French brasserie cuisine crafted by renowned French chefs, featuring escargot, croque monsieur, and crème brûlée
meals.dinner: Monsieur Paul in EPCOT France Pavilion — EPCOT's most elegant fine dining restaurant offering a sophisticated French tasting menu with an exceptional wine cellar and panoramic views of the lagoon

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT spans a large area — comfortable walking shoes are essential. Consider renting an EPCOT VIP tour guide for personalized cultural insights and skip-the-line access. The International Food & Wine Festival (typically August–November) would be a bonus if dates align.

day_by_day.morning: Hollywood Studios — Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Early Access: Leverage resort Early Entry to reach Galaxy's Edge before the masses. Begin with Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run for an interactive piloting experience. Then head to Rise of the Resistance — one of the most technologically advanced theme park attractions ever built — via Lightning Lane Individual.
day_by_day.afternoon: Savi's Workshop Lightsaber Building & Galaxy's Edge Exploration: Reserve a premium experience at Savi's Workshop to hand-build a custom lightsaber in an immersive, ceremony-driven experience (approximately $300 per saber). Explore Oga's Cantina for exotic themed cocktails and alien atmosphere. Visit Droid Depot to build a custom R-series or BB-series droid as a keepsake.
day_by_day.evening: Hollywood Studios — Fantasmic! & Tower of Terror: Experience the thrilling Tower of Terror and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster in the evening. Cap the night with Fantasmic! — Hollywood Studios' spectacular nighttime water, fire, and projection show. Upgrade to the Fantasmic! Dining Package for guaranteed premium reserved seating.

meals.breakfast: Sci-Fi Dine-In Theater Restaurant — a uniquely immersive Hollywood Studios experience where you dine in vintage cars watching classic sci-fi movie clips under a starlit indoor sky
meals.lunch: Oga's Cantina in Galaxy's Edge — exotic themed cocktails, specialty beverages, and light bites in the most immersive bar experience in any theme park on Earth
meals.dinner: Hollywood Brown Derby — the park's premier fine dining restaurant inspired by the legendary 1930s Hollywood icon, featuring the signature Cobb Salad prepared tableside and an award-winning wine list

day_by_day.notes: Savi's Workshop and Droid Depot require advance reservations and fill up extremely quickly — book at the 60-day mark. The Fantasmic! Dining Package includes guaranteed seating and is strongly recommended during peak June season. Budget approximately $300–$600 extra per person for Galaxy's Edge premium experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Animal Kingdom — Kilimanjaro Safaris at Dawn: Arrive at rope drop for Early Entry to Animal Kingdom. Head immediately to Kilimanjaro Safaris — the experience is most magical in the early morning when animals are most active in the cooler temperatures. Spot lions, elephants, giraffes, hippos, and rhinos in a stunning 110-acre African savanna setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Avatar: Flight of Passage & Pandora Exploration: Experience Avatar: Flight of Passage via Lightning Lane Individual — widely considered one of the greatest theme park attractions ever created, featuring a breathtaking banshee flight over the bioluminescent world of Pandora. Explore the Na'vi River Journey and the stunning Pandora landscape. Visit Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail and Maharajah Jungle Trek for up-close wildlife encounters.
day_by_day.evening: Tree of Life Awakenings & Animal Kingdom After Hours: As dusk falls, witness the Tree of Life Awakenings — a magical projection experience where the iconic 145-foot tree comes alive with glowing animal spirits. If Disney After Hours is available, enjoy the park in a near-empty, exclusive evening setting with complimentary snacks.

meals.breakfast: Tusker House Restaurant — a Disney character dining experience featuring Donald Duck and friends in safari attire, with a lavish African-inspired buffet including bobotie, pap, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Tiffins Restaurant — Animal Kingdom's flagship fine dining establishment offering globally inspired cuisine celebrating the spirit of world travel, with an exceptional wine and cocktail program and stunning art-filled interiors
meals.dinner: Jiko — The Cooking Place at Disney's Animal Kingdom Lodge (short transfer) — AAA Four Diamond restaurant featuring African-inspired cuisine, the largest collection of South African wines in the United States, and dramatic open-kitchen cooking theater

day_by_day.notes: Jiko at Animal Kingdom Lodge is one of the finest restaurants in all of Walt Disney World and requires advance reservations. Consider booking a savanna-view dinner at Boma or Sanaa at Animal Kingdom Lodge as an alternative. Animal Kingdom closes earlier than other parks — plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: VIP Tour Experience — Return to Favorite Parks: Book a Disney VIP Tour for the day (approximately $450–$900 per hour, 7-hour minimum) — a private guide provides skip-the-line access to all four parks, insider knowledge, and a fully customized experience. Use this premium service to revisit favorite attractions and experience anything missed earlier in the week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort Spa & Pool Relaxation: After an action-packed week, dedicate the afternoon to luxury relaxation. Indulge in treatments at a world-class Disney resort spa — consider the Grand Floridian Spa for signature massages, facials, and wellness therapies. Enjoy the resort pool with premium cabana service, cocktails, and light bites.
day_by_day.evening: Disney Springs Final Evening — Shopping & Celebration Dinner: Return to Disney Springs for a final evening of luxury shopping — visit UNIQLO, Anthropologie, Sugarboo & Co., and high-end boutiques. Browse the largest Disney merchandise location on property at World of Disney. Celebrate the penultimate evening with a spectacular farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: In-room premium breakfast service — arrange through concierge for a curated spread of fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, eggs prepared to order, fresh-squeezed juices, and specialty coffee delivered to your suite
meals.lunch: The Boathouse at Disney Springs — upscale waterfront dining featuring premium USDA dry-aged steaks, fresh Maine lobster, and raw bar selections with stunning amphicar and boat tour views
meals.dinner: STK Orlando at Disney Springs — a sophisticated modern steakhouse with USDA prime cuts, an innovative cocktail program, and a vibrant atmosphere; one of the most upscale non-Disney-operated restaurants on property

day_by_day.notes: VIP Tours must be booked well in advance by calling Disney's VIP Tour Services. This is the ultimate luxury Disney experience and transforms the entire park experience. Spa appointments at the Grand Floridian Spa should be reserved 30–60 days ahead. Use this day strategically to experience any missed must-dos.

day_by_day.morning: Final Magic Kingdom Visit — Farewell to the Magic: For a sentimental final morning, return to Magic Kingdom for one last Early Entry session. Ride any remaining bucket-list attractions, take photos on Main Street U.S.A. with Cinderella Castle, and soak in the atmosphere. Visit the Emporium for final souvenir shopping and pick up a custom-engraved keepsake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort Check-Out & Luxury Transfer: Complete a leisurely check-out with full bell service handling luggage. Arrange a private luxury vehicle transfer back to Orlando International Airport. Allow ample time for Orlando traffic and airport procedures — aim to depart the resort no later than 3–4 hours before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure: Enjoy airport lounge access before your flight. Reflect on an extraordinary week of premium Disney magic, world-class dining, and unforgettable family memories.

meals.breakfast: Steakhouse 71 at Disney's Contemporary Resort (walkable to Magic Kingdom) — a stylish breakfast inspired by Walt Disney World's opening year of 1971, featuring signature steak and eggs, brioche French toast, and premium coffee service
meals.lunch: The Plaza Restaurant on Main Street U.S.A., Magic Kingdom — a charming Victorian-era restaurant offering premium sandwiches, fresh salads, and elegant ice cream sundaes for a perfect farewell lunch inside the park
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining — arrange premium airport lounge access at MCO for a comfortable pre-departure experience with complimentary food and beverages

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-out (subject to availability) to maximize resort enjoyment before departure. Ship purchased merchandise directly home via Disney's package shipping service to avoid luggage hassles. Leave a generous gratuity for exceptional resort staff. Consider booking next year's trip before you leave — Disney's best discounts are often available for advance bookings made on property.

query: Disney World Orlando family of 4, $6000, 7 days, June 2026
